title: Performance
summary: Write queries the optimizer loves, code that never blows a limit, and UIs that load only what you need.

lessons.title: Limits You Must Know Cold
lessons.objective: Identify inefficiencies in code and how to resolve them (governor limits per transaction)

cards.body: Every Apex transaction gets a **budget**. Blow any line item and Salesforce throws a **LimitException** that you **cannot catch**.

cards.title: Sync vs Async (per transaction)
items: CPU time: **10,000 ms** sync / **60,000 ms** async
Heap: **10 MB** sync / **25 MB** async (older study guides say 6 / 12 MB)

cards.body: Async raises the **"brain" limits**: SOQL 100→200, heap 10→25 MB, CPU 10s→60s. DML (150), rows (50k), and callouts (100) **stay the same**.

cards.title: Check before you spend
cards.body: **Limits.getX()** = used so far. **Limits.getLimitX()** = the cap for this context.
try/catch does **not** rescue a LimitException. Design to stay under the limit; don't plan to recover from it.
Database time **does not** count toward CPU time. Loops, string building, JSON parsing and nested iterations **do**.

lessons.title: Bulkify or Bust
lessons.objective: Identify inefficiencies in code and how to resolve them (bulkification, collections)

cards.body: Triggers receive up to **200 records per chunk**. Code that queries or saves **per record** dies at record 101 (SOQL) or 151 (DML).

cards.title: The bulk recipe
items: 4. Loop again: change records in memory

cards.title: Map from a query
cards.body: The Map constructor keys records by Id. No extra loop needed.

cards.title: SOQL for loop = heap saver
cards.body: Records stream in chunks of 200, so the whole result never sits in the heap at once.
SOQL for loops save **heap**, not **rows**. Every row still counts toward the **50,000** row limit.
Mnemonic **"No Q in the Loop, No D in the Loop"**: no Queries, no DML inside for loops.

lessons.title: Selective Queries & Indexes
lessons.objective: Identify performance issues and mitigation techniques for SOQL queries on large data volumes

cards.body: A query is **selective** when an **indexed** filter cuts the rows down below a threshold. Then the optimizer uses the index instead of scanning the whole table.

cards.title: Thresholds (single filter)
items: **Standard** index: < **30%** of first 1M rows + **15%** beyond, max **1,000,000**
**Custom** index: < **10%** of first 1M rows + **5%** beyond, max **333,333**

cards.body: **"30-15 standard, 10-5 custom."** Standard indexes are trusted 3x more.

cards.title: Need a custom index?
cards.body: Mark a field **External ID** or **Unique** to index it yourself. Otherwise ask **Salesforce Support** for a custom index.
In a **trigger**, a non-selective query on an object with **more than 200,000 rows** throws **"Non-selective query against large object type"**. Big orgs need selective trigger queries.

lessons.title: Query Plan & Index Killers
lessons.objective: Identify performance issues and mitigation techniques for SOQL queries (Query Plan tool, optimizer behavior)

cards.body: Turn on the **Query Plan** tool in Developer Console preferences. It shows each plan the optimizer considered with a **Cost**.
**Cost < 1 = selective.** Cost > 1 = not selective. Lower is better. Look for "Index" vs "TableScan" in Leading Operation Type.

cards.title: Index killers
items: Comparing to **null** on a custom-indexed field
Complex OR where any branch is unindexed

cards.body: Custom indexes **skip null values** by default. `WHERE Region__c = null` cannot use the custom index unless Support builds one that includes nulls.

cards.title: Skinny tables
cards.body: Salesforce Support can build a **skinny table**: a narrow copy of frequently used fields from **one object**, kept in sync automatically. Fewer joins, faster reads. Up to **100 columns**.
Skinny tables **can't** include fields from other objects, and they are copied only to **Full** sandboxes automatically.

lessons.title: Large Data Volumes & Skew
lessons.objective: Identify performance issues and mitigation techniques for large data volumes (data skew, sharing, loading)

cards.body: **Data skew** = too many records piled on one owner or parent. Salesforce flags trouble at about **10,000 records** per owner or parent.

cards.title: Three flavors of skew
items: **Ownership skew**: one user owns >10k records of an object
**Lookup skew**: huge numbers of records point to one lookup record

cards.title: Why it hurts
cards.body: Updating a child **locks the parent**. Many parallel updates on one parent = **lock contention** (UNABLE_TO_LOCK_ROW). Moving a skewed owner in the role hierarchy triggers **massive sharing recalculation**.
Skewed owner? Put them in **no role**, or a role at the **top of the hierarchy** with no subordinates. Skewed parent? **Spread** children across more parents.

cards.title: Loading millions of rows
items: Sort load files by **parent Id** to reduce lock contention
Switch to **serial mode** if locks persist

cards.title: Big Objects
cards.body: Billions of rows that rarely change (audit, history)? Use **Big Objects**: query by their **index fields** only, in order.

lessons.title: Cache It, Don't Re-Fetch It
lessons.objective: Identify inefficiencies in code and how to resolve them (caching, describes, CPU)

cards.title: Static lazy-load
cards.body: Query once per **transaction**, reuse everywhere. Statics live only for the transaction.

cards.title: Platform Cache
items: **Org cache**: shared by all users, survives across transactions
**Session cache**: per user session, max 8 hours
Both live in **partitions** you allocate in Setup

cards.body: Always handle a **cache miss**. Items can be evicted any time.
Session cache is **not available in async Apex** (batch, future). Use org cache there.

cards.title: CPU savers
items: Avoid repeated **Schema.getGlobalDescribe()**; use **Account.SObjectType.getDescribe()** or cache results
Stop **trigger recursion** with a static guard

lessons.title: Snappy Lightning Web Components
lessons.objective: Identify common performance issues for user interfaces and techniques to resolve them

cards.title: Cacheable Apex
cards.body: Required for **@wire**. Results are cached on the client, so repeat calls skip the server.
A **cacheable=true** method **cannot do DML**. After data changes, call **refreshApex()** on the wired property to get fresh data.

cards.title: Lightning Data Service
cards.body: Use **lightning-record-form**, **getRecord** and other **LDS** adapters for single records. They share **one cache** across components and need **no Apex**.

cards.title: Load less, later
items: **lwc:if** to render heavy sections only when needed
**Pagination** or **infinite loading** instead of thousands of rows

cards.title: Infinite loading
cards.body: **loadMore** fetches the next page and appends it. Set **isLoading** while fetching.
SOQL **OFFSET** maxes out at **2,000**. For deep paging use **keyset**: `WHERE Id > :lastId ORDER BY Id LIMIT 50`.

lessons.title: Visualforce on a Diet
lessons.objective: Identify common performance issues for user interfaces and techniques to resolve them (Visualforce)

cards.body: **View state** = the serialized controller state posted back with every **apex:form** request. Max size: **170 KB**.

cards.title: transient
cards.body: **transient** fields are not saved in view state. Recompute them when needed.

cards.title: readOnly="true"
cards.body: On **apex:page**, it lifts SOQL row retrieval to **1,000,000** and iteration to **10,000** items, but the page **cannot do DML**.
You **can't** raise the 170 KB view state limit. Not even Support can. Fix the page.
Use the **View State** tab in the Development Mode footer to find the heaviest variables.

lessons.title: Right Query, Right Place
lessons.objective: Identify performance issues and mitigation techniques for queries and long-running processes (SOSL vs SOQL, aggregates, async)

cards.title: SOSL vs SOQL
items: **SOSL**: text search across **many objects** at once, uses the search index
**SOQL**: exact filters on **known fields** of one object (plus relationships)
SOSL returns max **2,000** rows per query

cards.title: Aggregate instead of looping
cards.body: The database does the math. Less heap, far less CPU.

cards.title: Polymorphic TYPEOF
cards.code:
SELECT Id, Subject,
  TYPEOF What
    WHEN Account THEN Name, Phone
    WHEN Opportunity THEN Name, Amount
  END
FROM Task
cards.body: Pull different fields depending on the **type** of a polymorphic lookup.
TYPEOF can't be used with **GROUP BY**/**HAVING**, can't be nested, and isn't supported in **Bulk API** queries.

cards.title: Offload heavy work
items: **Queueable**: chainable, takes objects, can do callouts
**Batch Apex**: millions of rows, fresh limits per chunk
**Platform Events**: decouple, subscriber runs in its own transaction
